newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Short recent chronology of Russian rouble.
newsitem.headline: Short recent chronology of Russian rouble.

text.p: Here is a short chronology of the Russian rouble, whose redomination was announced on Monday.
August 4, 1997 - President Boris Yeltsin says a new rouble worth 1,000 old roubles will be introduced on January 1, 1998, underscoring the government's success in taming inflation.
Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin says currency policy is unchanged and that the rouble will probably continue to devalue roughly in line with inflation next year.
The rouble trades at 5,799 per dollar on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), up from 5,805 on Friday.
November 26, 1996 - Central bank announces currency "corridor" for 1997 -- rouble to to depreciate from 5,500-6,100 range on January 1 to 5,750-6,350 on December 31. (Rouble 5,497 on MICEX).
May 31, 1996 - Russia signs Article Eight of the IMF, making the rouble convertible for current account transactions. (Rouble 5,031 on MICEX)
May 16, 1996 - Yeltsin signs decree on steps towards making the rouble fully convertible.

Russia sets rouble corridor for second half of 1996, moving from 5,000-5,600 on July 1 to 5,500-6,100 on December 31. Central bank to set daily buying and selling rates for rouble within corridor, effectively introducing a crawling rouble-dollar peg. (Rouble 4,970 on MICEX)
November 30, 1995 - Russia sets 4,550-5,150 rouble corridor for first half of 1996. (Rouble 4,580 on MICEX)
August 24, 1995 - Widespread banking crisis starts. Newly stable rouble one factor, as banks can no longer make easy profits speculating in currency market. (Rouble 4,428 on MICEX).

July 5, 1995 - Russia introduces a "rouble corridor" with upper and lower limits of 4,900 and 4,300 per dollar respectively running to end of year, backed by $10 billion in central bank reserves. (Rouble 4,559 on MICEX).
The move follows a stabilisation of the rouble in early 1995, helped by high yields on the Treasury bill market.
October 11, 1994 - Rouble falls about 30 percent on "Black Tuesday" to 3,926 per dollar on MICEX from 3,081.
July 6, 1994 - Rouble falls below 2,000 per dollar
January 19, 1994 - The rouble loses almost 30 percent in first 19 days of year as prominent reformers Boris Fyodorov and Yegor Gaidar quit government. (Rouble 1,607 on MICEX)
October 1993 - Bloody showdown between Yeltsin and his parliamentary foes has little influence on rouble rate.
July 24, 1993 - Old roubles withdrawn from circulation. (Rouble 1,004 on MICEX)
May 1993 - Rouble breaks below 1,000 to the dollar amid concern about Russia's inflationary outlook.
1992 - Rouble halves in value to 205 per dollar in August from 112 in June as overall economic outlook worsens. Ends year at 414.50
Early 1992 -- Moscow Interbank Commercial Exchange (MICEX) opens. Rouble stands at 160.30 per dollar.
December 1991-January 1992 -- Radical market reforms start under acting premier Yegor Gaidar after fall of Soviet Union.
1989 - Street trade comes to life in 1989, dollar fetches anything from 15 to 25 roubles with official rate still about 1 to 1.

During 1980s dollar fetches about 60 kopecks. All currency deals are banned by law and severely punished by up to 15 years in labour camps or even by death penalty, depending on sums involved. But the last man sentenced to death for currency speculation was in the 1950s under Nikita Khrushchev.
Russians could buy 200 dollars per head if going abroad during Soviet period. A handful of state banks were allowed to trade in dollars.
